Traditional NetOps

→

Nile Autonomous Operations

  • AI Topology with Digital Twin

    Models the network topology, plans cabling and fabric IP addressing, and prepares hardware sizing and the equipment list for approval.

  • AI-assisted service bring-up

    Hardware and software come online automatically at the site, eliminating separate staging. Autonomous Ops applies and validates configurations and sets the initial Wi‑Fi channel and radio settings.

  • AI-based activation & validation

    Nile Nav uses AI to guide installation and activation, validate the deployment against the approved design, and produce as-built documentation.

  • AI-assisted integration & cutover

    Nile services simplify integrations such as RADIUS, NAC, DHCP, DNS, and firewalls. Deployment checks support acceptance testing and cutover.

Closed-loop AI Automation

From detection to verified recovery.

Autonomous Operations uses live network data, AI agents, and the Digital Twin to resolve supported issues within your policies.

See closed-loop AI Automation in action ↗
Detect Diagnose Remediate Validate Learn Operational intelligence

Detect

Infrastructure, wireless, and user-experience signals reveal deviations from normal or intended operation.

Diagnose

AI RCA (root-cause analysis) correlates events and uses digital-twin context to identify the cause, affected services, and appropriate response.

Remediate

Automated workflows correct the condition, restore connectivity, or tune performance. Service-impacting changes follow your approval requirements.

Validate

Fresh telemetry and digital-twin checks confirm the result. Unresolved conditions remain open for further diagnosis or Nile service intervention.

Learn

Validated outcomes feed the intelligence behind Autonomous Operations. Recurring issues are matched to known patterns, scored by impact, and linked to permanent fixes. Those fixes roll out as part of the service, so every customer benefits.

Closed-loop AI Automation in practice

Keep traffic moving when a link degrades.

Follow traffic from the preferred uplink to the alternate path and back.

Published Nile demo

What happens to traffic during recovery

Watch Nile’s uplink demo ↗
  1. Detect

    An abnormal rise in CRC errors signals that data is arriving corrupted on a fabric uplink.

  2. Diagnose

    Autonomous Ops identifies the degraded path and opens an incident with diagnostic context.

  3. Remediate

    Raising the affected link’s routing cost shifts traffic to a healthy parallel path.

  4. Validate

    Autonomous Ops monitors the link and restores the preferred route once the link is stable.

If the issue recurs, Autonomous Ops links the events and alerts IT when hands-on repair is needed.

Learn in practice

A fix at one site can protect others.

When a software vulnerability is found at one site, Autonomous Ops can identify other Nile-managed sites running the affected version, prioritize patching by impact, and verify service health after rollout.

More use cases

Wi‑Fi experience

Keep Wi‑Fi working at busy sites

When Wi‑Fi performance drops, Autonomous Ops correlates radio conditions with user experience. It can adjust radio or channel settings within policy and verify recovery.

Software upgrades

Upgrade software in planned windows

Autonomous Ops checks readiness, rolls out approved upgrades in agreed maintenance windows, and verifies service health. Exceptions are flagged for review.

Network resilience

Restore connectivity after a link or tunnel fails

When a link or tunnel fails, Autonomous Ops checks the affected path and available redundancy, triggers supported failover or recovery, and verifies connectivity.

Configuration drift

Keep the network aligned with the approved design

The Digital Twin shows where live configurations differ from the approved design. Autonomous Ops restores the intended settings within policy and approval requirements, then verifies the correction.

A few practical answers

Your questions,
answered.

What makes Nile Autonomous Operations different?

Nile Autonomous Operations is built into the network service. For supported issues, it diagnoses the cause, applies authorized fixes, and verifies recovery.

Does autonomous mean no people are involved?

No. Monitoring, diagnosis, optimization, and closed-loop remediation are automated. Physical installation, hardware work, unresolved exceptions, and service-impacting changes can require specialist involvement or customer approval. Nile and its delivery partners provide the service expertise around AI Automation.

What if an automated action does not resolve the issue?

The issue needs further diagnosis or service intervention. Nile-managed infrastructure issues remain within the service responsibility defined in your agreement. Dependencies outside that boundary are coordinated with the responsible customer or third-party team.

Does this operate all of my existing network equipment?

This page describes operations for Nile-managed wired and wireless infrastructure. It does not imply autonomous control of all third-party equipment, firewalls, applications, or internet services. Discuss migration and integration scope with Nile.

How are software upgrades handled?

Autonomous Ops rolls out approved upgrades in agreed maintenance windows, checks service health before and after, and flags exceptions for review.
